title: Load timestamp enrichment data from recorded item attachments
description:
Implement the behavior specified by story plx-b0cab6.

Plan:
- Add a focused failing test around LangGraph timestamp enrichment when Deepgram exists only as an Item attachment key.
- Update enrichment to resolve a Deepgram attachment from explicit metadata/attached files before falling back to legacy key guessing.
- Run the focused test and relevant timestamp tests.

comments.author: ec2-user
comments.text: Starting test-first implementation. Current understanding: when Deepgram is only available as an Item attachment, enrichment should load the recorded attachment key instead of deriving a storage key from the Item id. First step is to add a focused failing test that captures this behavior without client-specific data.

comments.author: ec2-user
comments.text: Added failing spec `test_timestamp_enrichment_uses_recorded_deepgram_attachment_key`. The red result confirms the suspected failure mode: enrichment currently asks for `items/{item_id}/deepgram.json` even when metadata contains the actual Item attachment key. Next step is to resolve Deepgram from explicit attachment references before falling back to legacy key guessing.

comments.author: ec2-user
comments.text:
Implemented focused fix and verification.

Changes:
- Added failing-then-passing LangGraph spec proving enrichment must use recorded Item attachment keys instead of deriving `items/{item_id}/deepgram.json`.
- Updated LangGraph timestamp enrichment to resolve Deepgram from explicit metadata pointers and `attachedFiles`/`attached_files`/attachment dictionaries before legacy path fallback.
- Updated the lambda score processor to pass `Item.attachedFiles` into scoring metadata.
- Added lambda processor test proving attached file keys are handed to scoring metadata.

Verification:
- `conda run -n py311 python -m pytest plexus/scores/LangGraphScore_test.py -k recorded_deepgram_attachment_key -q` passed.
- `conda run -n py311 python -m pytest tests/test_score_result_timestamps.py tests/test_scoring_single_target_helper.py -q` passed: 12 passed.
- `conda run -n py311 env PYTHONPATH=score-processor-lambda python -m pytest score-processor-lambda/tests/test_handler.py -q` passed: 7 passed.

comments.author: ec2-user
comments.text:
Ran Docker lambda smoke test locally with Docker requiring sudo.

Commands:
- `sudo docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --load -f score-processor-lambda/Dockerfile -t score-processor-lambda:latest .`
- `sudo docker run --rm -v /home/ec2-user/projects/Plexus/score-processor-lambda/tests/smoke_test.py:/var/task/smoke_test.py --entrypoint python score-processor-lambda:latest smoke_test.py`

Result: container smoke test passed, 10 passed / 0 failed. Noted non-fatal CloudWatch warning from intentionally fake AWS test credentials during import.

comments.author: ec2-user
comments.text: Implementing follow-up fallback for recorded attachment reads when an item-style attachment key is stored in the score-result attachments bucket rather than the datasource bucket. No client-specific identifiers included.

comments.author: ec2-user
comments.text: Added fallback behavior for item-style attachment reads: the downloader now tries the datasource bucket first, then the score-result attachments bucket when the datasource bucket returns not found. Focused utility tests cover fallback, non-item routing, and non-not-found errors. Tactus and LangGraph attachment regressions passed locally; a read-only live SDK spot check was blocked by the local conda boto credential dependency, while AWS CLI verified the production object exists.

comments.author: ec2-user
comments.text: Local timestamp proof with a real Deepgram JSON fixture exposed an additional Tactus runtime issue: enrichment Lua needed to be wrapped as a Procedure. Updated TactusScore enrichment accordingly and added a real-runtime regression. Verified local enrichment returns bracketed spans and parsed seconds, and focused Tactus/LangGraph/bucket-routing tests pass.
